messages.author: fd2046a1a7c5fa91
messages.subject: Reliability Decomposition for Common Method Variance test (Williams et al. 2010)
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am struggling to compute the reliability decomposition following Williams et al. (2010, see citation at end of post).

Does someone have an example of how to do this correctly? I don’t understand which specific factor loadings and error variances I need to extract and use from the lavaan object. In the paper (p. 500), it merely says:

(2) R_sub = (sum substantive factor ldgs)^2 / [(sum substantive factor ldgs)^2 + (sum method factor ldgs)^2 + sum error variances]

(3) R_meth = (sum method factor ldgs)^2 / [(sum substantive factor ldgs)^2 + (sum method factor ldgs)^2 + sum error variances]


Please see my failed attempt(s) below:
```
  base.model <- "
          # ... rest of model ...
          connectivity_maturity_lat =~ connectivity_maturity_1 + connectivity_maturity_3 + connectivity_maturity_4
          # ...
          marker_jazz_lat =~ latent_marker_jazz
          # ... rest of model ..."

  model_c <- "# ..."   # same model as base.model with substantive factor correlations restricted to values obtained with the baseline model

  fit.base <- sem(base.model, df, estimator="MLR", missing="FIML", fixed.x=F)
  fit.c <- sem(model_c, df, estimator="MLR", missing="FIML", fixed.x=F)

  # Total reliability from baseline model
  df.loadings <- as.data.frame(inspect(fit.base, what="std")$lambda)
  df.errors <- as.data.frame(inspect(fit.base, what="std")$theta)

  factor.loadings.sum <- df.loadings %>% select(connectivity_maturity_lat) %>% sum()
  factor.errors.sum <- df.errors %>% select(connectivity_maturity_1, connectivity_maturity_3, connectivity_maturity_4) %>% sum()
  reliability.total <- factor.loadings.sum^2 / (factor.loadings.sum^2 + factor.errors.sum)

  # substantive and method reliability from model c or u (fit.c)
  df.loadings <- as.data.frame(inspect(fit.c, what="std")$lambda)
  df.errors <- as.data.frame(inspect(fit.c, what="std")$theta)
  factor.loadings.sum <- df.loadings %>% select(connectivity_maturity_lat) %>% filter(row.names(df.loadings) %in% c("connectivity_maturity_1", "connectivity_maturity_3", "connectivity_maturity_4")) %>% sum()
  factor.errors.sum <- df.errors %>% select(connectivity_maturity_1, connectivity_maturity_3, connectivity_maturity_4, latent_marker_jazz) %>% filter(row.names(df.errors) %in% c("connectivity_maturity_1", "connectivity_maturity_3", "connectivity_maturity_4", "latent_marker_jazz")) %>% sum()

  # try 1
  factor.methodvar.sum <- df.loadings %>% select(marker_jazz_lat) %>% filter(row.names(df.loadings) %in% c("latent_marker_jazz")) %>% sum()
  # try 2
  factor.methodvar.sum <- df.loadings %>% select(marker_jazz_lat) %>% filter(row.names(df.loadings) %in% c("connectivity_maturity_1", "connectivity_maturity_3", "connectivity_maturity_4")) %>% sum()
  # try 3
  factor.methodvar.sum <- df.loadings %>% select(marker_jazz_lat) %>% filter(row.names(df.loadings) %in% c("connectivity_maturity_1", "connectivity_maturity_3", "connectivity_maturity_4", "latent_marker_jazz")) %>% sum()

  reliability.sub <- factor.loadings.sum^2 / (factor.loadings.sum^2 + factor.methodvar.sum^2 + factor.errors.sum)
  reliability.meth <- factor.methodvar.sum^2 / (factor.loadings.sum^2 + factor.methodvar.sum^2 + factor.errors.sum)

  results <- cbind(reliability.total, reliability.sub, reliability.meth, reliability.sub + reliability.meth, reliability.meth/reliability.total)
  colnames(results) <- c("Total Reliability", "Substantive Reliability", "Method Reliability", "Checkvalue", "% Reliability Marker")

  results
#      Total Reliability Substantive Reliability Method Reliability Checkvalue % Reliability Marker
# [1,]         0.6883293               0.4820782          0.1664716  0.6485499            0.2418488
```

As you can see, the values do not make sense because R_tot = R_sub + R_meth should hold. I guess I do not fully understand the theory behind the Williams et al. (2010) approach. 

Any help for my specific issue or just an example with data and code to reproduce would be highly appreciated.

Thank you, and kind regards,

Williams, L. J., Hartman, N., & Cavazotte, F. (2010). Method variance and marker variables: A review and comprehensive CFA marker technique. Organizational research methods, 13(3), 477-514. https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/1094428110366036
